nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of CdS nanorods
nodes.procedure: 0.95 g of Cd(NO3)2·4H2O and 0.71 g of NH2CSNH2 were dispersed into 25 mL of ethylenediamine under magnetic stirring for 30 min, and then the solution was transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and maintained at 160 °C for 12 h. After being cooled naturally to room temperature, the yellow powders were centrifuged, washed with distilled water, and then dried in air at 60 °C.

nodes.name: One-step calcination synthesis of heterostructures
nodes.procedure: 0.06 g of dicyandiamide (C2H4N4) and 0.2 g of prepared CdS nanorods were thoroughly ground in an agate mortar for 10 min, and then 0.06 g of ammonium metatungstate (H28N6O41W12·H2O) was added and ground for another 10 min. The final solid mixture was first heated to 400 °C for 0.5 h at a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹, and then treated at 800 °C at a heating rate of 5 °C min⁻¹ under a N2 atmosphere for 5 h. The flow rate of N2 was strictly controlled at 5 mL min⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure CdS indexed to hexagonal phase (PDF#77-2306); WWC-1–6 shows additional 2H-WS2 peaks at 14.4°, 32.8°, 33.6° for (002), (100), (101) planes; (002) peak widens with increasing dicyandiamide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks of pure CdS can be indexed to the hexagonal phase (PDF#77-2306). Compared with that of pure CdS, the diffraction peaks of WWC-1–6 at 14.4, 32.8, and 33.6° are ascribed to the (002), (100), and (101) crystal planes of 2H-WS2 (PDF#84-1398)... with the increase of added dicyandiamide, the diffraction peak of the (002) crystal plane gets widened.

nodes.characterization_summary: Two prominent peaks for E2g¹ and A1g modes of 2H-WS2; peak at 173 cm⁻¹ (J₁) reveals presence of 1T phase WS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides the Raman features of CdS, two prominent peaks corresponding to the in-plane E2g¹ and out-of-plane A1g modes of 2H-WS2 nanosheets are observed... the peak of WWC-1–6 at 173 cm⁻¹ (J₁) reveals the presence of 1T phase WS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: WWC-1–6 shows peaks at 1380 and 1468 cm⁻¹ due to W–S band bending and stretching vibrations, and 3420 cm⁻¹ for H2O and O–H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for WWC-1–6, the peaks at 1380 and 1468 cm⁻¹ are due to the W–S band bending and stretching vibrations, and the peak at 3420 cm⁻¹ is indexed to the bending and stretching vibrations of H2O and O–H.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type-IV isotherms; BET surface areas: pure CdS 37.76 m²/g, WWC-1–6 111.51 m²/g, pure WS2 141.36 m²/g; pore volumes: pure CdS 0.05 cm³/g, WWC-1–6 0.23 cm³/g, pure WS2 0.31 cm³/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 adsorption–desorption isotherms of pure CdS, WWC-1–6, and pure WS2 display typical type-IV isotherms... the BET surface areas of pure CdS, WWC-1–6, and pure WS2 are 37.76, 111.51, and 141.36 m² g⁻¹, and the pore volumes are 0.05, 0.23, and 0.31 cm³ g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CdS nanorods ~20 nm diameter exposing (110) planes (0.206 nm spacing); WS2 nanosheets on CdS show 2H-(100) planes (0.273 nm) and 1T-phase with 0.938 nm layer spacing (vs 0.622 nm for 2H-phase); SAED shows dominant (110) CdS and (100) WS2 planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The prepared CdS samples present uniform rod-like nanostructures with a diameter of about 20 nm, exposing (110) crystal planes with a lattice spacing of 0.206 nm... the (100) crystal planes of the 2H-phase WS2 nanosheets with a lattice spacing of 0.273 nm were mainly exposed... 1T-phase with a distinct layer spacing of 0.938 nm is different from that of 0.622 nm of the 2H-phase... the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern also suggests dominant (110) and (100) crystal planes for CdS nanorods and WS2 nanosheets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cd 3d peaks shift to higher binding energies (412.01, 405.27 eV); W 4f shows 1T-WS2 at 34.18/31.95 eV and 2H-WS2 at 35.02/32.66 eV; 1T phase ratio ~39.12%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cd 3d peaks of WWC-1–6 shift to higher binding energies of 412.01 and 405.27 eV... the peaks at 34.18 and 31.95 eV can be ascribed to W 4f5/2 and W 4f7/2 of 1T-WS2, and the peaks at 35.02 and 32.66 eV belong to W 4f5/2 and W 4f7/2 of 2H-WS2... the ratio of the 1T phase in WWC-1–6 is about 39.12%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong signal at g=2.004 belonging to sulfur vacancies in WWC-1–6, absent in pure CdS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There is a strong signal at the Lorentzian line with g = 2.004 belonging to sulfur vacancies in WWC-1–6, which is absent in pure CdS.

nodes.characterization_summary: WWC-1–6 bandgap 1.77 eV (vs 2.41 eV for CdS); well-resolved absorption band 575-675 nm due to 1T-WS2 LSPR effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bandgap has decreased from 2.41 eV (CdS) to 1.77 eV (WWC-1–6). The splendid plasmonic effect of 1T-WS2 endows WWC-1–6 with a well-resolved absorption band between 575 and 675 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution imaging confirms WS2 nanosheets with both 1T and 2H phases loaded on stable CdS nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the calcination process, WS2 nanosheets with both 1T and 2H phases were successfully loaded on CdS nanorods... It can be seen that CdS has good stability by keeping the one-dimensional nanorods unchanged.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows W mainly at nanosheet edges, Cd distributed centrally as rods, S uniformly throughout WWC-1–6 heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping illustrates that W is mainly distributed at the edge of nanosheets, Cd is distributed centrally as a rod shape, and sulfur is distributed uniformly throughout 1T-WS2/2H-WS2/CdS heterostructures (WWC-1–6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction pattern suggests dominant (110) planes for CdS nanorods and (100) planes for WS2 nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern also suggests dominant (110) and (100) crystal planes for CdS nanorods and WS2 nanosheets, respectively.
